sanskrit: arthavanty upapannāni vākyāni guṇavanti ca naiva saṃprāpnuvanti tvāṃ mumūrṣum iva bheṣajam
english: Words full of meaning, well-reasoned and rich in virtue — they do not reach you, just as medicine fails to reach one who is dying.

sanskrit: santi vai sindhurājasya saṃtuṣṭā bahavo janāḥ daurbalyād āsate mūḍhā vyasanaughapratīkṣiṇaḥ
english: Indeed, many people are content with the king of the Sindhus; foolishly, out of weakness, they sit awaiting a flood of misfortune.

sanskrit: sahāyopacayaṃ kṛtvā vyavasāyya tatas tataḥ anuduṣyeyur apare paśyantas tava pauruṣam
english: After gathering supporters and resolving your course step by step, others will cease to find fault, seeing your manliness.

sanskrit: taiḥ kṛtvā saha saṃghātaṃ giridurgālayāṃś cara kāle vyasanam ākāṅkṣan naivāyam ajarāmaraḥ
english: Having allied with them, roam the mountain fastnesses; awaiting the enemy's moment of adversity, for he is not immortal and undying.

sanskrit: saṃjayo nāmataś ca tvaṃ na ca paśyāmi tat tvayi anvarthanāmā bhava me putra mā vyarthanāmakaḥ
english: You bear the name Sañjaya — 'he who conquers completely' — yet I do not see that quality in you. Live up to your name, my son; do not let it be an empty name.

sanskrit: samyagdṛṣṭir mahāprājño bālaṃ tvāṃ brāhmaṇo 'bravīt ayaṃ prāpya mahat kṛcchraṃ punar vṛddhiṃ gamiṣyati
english: A brahmin of keen sight and great wisdom spoke thus of you when you were a child: 'This one, having passed through great hardship, will rise again to prosperity.'

sanskrit: tasya smarantī vacanam āśaṃse vijayaṃ tava tasmāt tāta bravīmi tvāṃ vakṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Remembering his words, I hope for your victory. That is why, my dear, I speak to you now and will speak to you again and again.

sanskrit: yasya hy arthābhinirvṛttau bhavanty āpyāyitāḥ pare tasyārthasiddhir niyatā nayeṣv arthānusāriṇaḥ
english: He in whose accomplishment of goals others are enriched — for him who follows statecraft's path, success in his aims is assured.

sanskrit: samṛddhir asamṛddhir vā pūrveṣāṃ mama saṃjaya evaṃ vidvān yuddhamanā bhava mā pratyupāhara
english: Whether prosperity or adversity came to those before us, my Sañjaya — knowing this, be battle-minded; do not retreat.

sanskrit: nātaḥ pāpīyasīṃ kāṃ cid avasthāṃ śambaro 'bravīt yatra naivādya na prātar bhojanaṃ pratidṛśyate
english: Śambara declared there is no more wretched condition than that in which no food is seen — not today, not tomorrow morning.

sanskrit: patiputravadhād etat paramaṃ duḥkham abravīt dāridryam iti yat proktaṃ paryāyamaraṇaṃ hi tat
english: He said this surpasses even the grief of losing husband and son; what is called poverty is indeed death by instalments.

sanskrit: ahaṃ mahākule jātā hradād dhradam ivāgatā īśvarī sarvakalyāṇair bhartrā paramapūjitā
english: I was born in a great lineage, passed from one fine pool to another like water; a mistress of all auspiciousness, supremely honoured by my husband.

sanskrit: mahārhamālyābharaṇāṃ sumṛṣṭāmbaravāsasam purā dṛṣṭvā suhṛdvargo mām apaśyat sudurgatām
english: Adorned once with costly garlands and jewels, dressed in fine, bright garments — now the circle of friends who knew me thus sees me utterly fallen.

sanskrit: yadā māṃ caiva bhāryāṃ ca draṣṭāsi bhṛśadurbale na tadā jīvitenārtho bhavitā tava saṃjaya
english: When you see both me and your wife reduced to extreme weakness, then life will hold no worth for you, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: dāsakarmakarān bhṛtyān ācāryartvik purohitān avṛttyāsmān prajahato dṛṣṭvā kiṃ jīvitena te
english: Seeing slaves, labourers, servants, teachers, officiants, and priests abandon us for want of livelihood — what good is life to you then?

sanskrit: yadi kṛtyaṃ na paśyāmi tavādyeha yathā purā ślāghanīyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: If I cannot see you doing here today what is praiseworthy and glorious, as in former times, what peace can there be for my heart?

sanskrit: neti ced brāhmaṇān brūyāṃ dīryate hṛdayaṃ mama na hy ahaṃ na ca me bhartā neti brāhmaṇam uktavān
english: If I were forced to say 'no' to brahmins, my heart would shatter — for neither I nor my husband has ever said 'no' to a brahmin.

sanskrit: vayam āśrayaṇīyāḥ sma nāśritāraḥ parasya ca sānyān āśritya jīvantī parityakṣyāmi jīvitam
english: We were ones others took refuge in, not those who sheltered under another's roof. I — who must now live depending on strangers — will give up life itself.

sanskrit: apāre bhava naḥ pāram aplave bhava naḥ plavaḥ kuruṣva sthānam asthāne mṛtān saṃjīvayasva naḥ
english: Be a far shore for us who have no shore; be a raft for us who have no boat; make a place where there is none; bring us back to life from the dead.

sanskrit: sarve te śatravaḥ sahyā na cej jīvitum icchasi atha ced īdṛśīṃ vṛttiṃ klībām abhyupapadyase
english: All your enemies are endurable — if you do not wish to go on living; but if you adopt this cowardly way of life instead —

sanskrit: nirviṇṇātmā hatamanā muñcaitāṃ pāpajīvikām ekaśatruvadhenaiva śūro gacchati viśrutim
english: — with your spirit crushed and your courage slain, then abandon this sinful existence: by slaying even a single enemy, a hero attains great renown.

sanskrit: indro vṛtravadhenaiva mahendraḥ samapadyata māhendraṃ ca grahaṃ lebhe lokānāṃ ceśvaro 'bhavat
english: By slaying Vṛtra alone, Indra became the great Indra; he obtained the Mahendra asterism and became the lord of all the worlds.

sanskrit: nāma viśrāvya vā saṃkhye śatrūn āhūya daṃśitān senāgraṃ vāpi vidrāvya hatvā vā puruṣaṃ varam
english: Whether by proclaiming his name on the battlefield, or by challenging armoured foes, or by routing the van of an army, or by slaying a great warrior —

sanskrit: yadaiva labhate vīraḥ suyuddhena mahad yaśaḥ tadaiva pravyathante 'sya śatravo vinamanti ca
english: — the very moment a hero wins great glory through noble combat, his enemies are filled with dread and bow before him.

sanskrit: tyaktvātmānaṃ raṇe dakṣaṃ śūraṃ kāpuruṣā janāḥ avaśāḥ pūrayanti sma sarvakāmasamṛddhibhiḥ
english: Cowards, unable to help themselves, heap every desired wealth upon a skilled and valiant hero who has abandoned all care for his own life in battle.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ vāpy ugravibhraṃśaṃ saṃśayo jīvitasya vā pralabdhasya hi śatror vai śeṣaṃ kurvanti sādhavaḥ
english: Even when the kingdom is utterly lost or life itself is in doubt, noble men make sure the deceiving enemy does not escape — they leave him no remainder.

sanskrit: svargadvāropamaṃ rājyam atha vāpy amṛtopamam ruddham ekāyane matvā patolmuka ivāriṣu
english: Regarding a kingdom — equal to the gateway of heaven, or equal to nectar — as something blocked on a single narrow path, move against your enemies like a blazing torch.

sanskrit: jahi śatrūn raṇe rājan svadharmam anupālaya mā tvā paśyet sukṛpaṇaṃ śatruḥ śrīmān kadā cana
english: Slay your enemies in battle, O king; uphold your own duty. Never let a prosperous enemy see you pitifully wretched.

sanskrit: asmadīyaiś ca śocadbhir nadadbhiś ca parair vṛtam api tvāṃ nānupaśyeyaṃ dīnā dīnam avasthitam
english: Even though wretched myself, I would not wish to see you surrounded by our own people weeping and your enemies exulting, standing there in misery.

sanskrit: uṣya sauvīrakanyābhiḥ ślāghasvārthair yathā purā mā ca saindhavakanyānām avasan no vaśaṃ gamaḥ
english: Dwell with the girls of Sauvīra; pursue your aims with pride as in former times; do not, while dwelling there, fall under the sway of the Saindhava maidens.

sanskrit: yuvā rūpeṇa saṃpanno vidyayābhijanena ca yas tvādṛśo vikurvīta yaśasvī lokaviśrutaḥ voḍhavye dhury anaḍuvan manye maraṇam eva tat
english: A young man endowed with beauty, learning, and noble birth — one of your calibre who is famous and widely renowned — if such a one behaves dishonourably, then I deem it death for a bull of burden to flinch from the yoke it should bear.

sanskrit: yadi tvām anupaśyāmi parasya priyavādinam pṛṣṭhato 'nuvrajantaṃ vā kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: If I were to see you speaking pleasant words to another's man and following at his heels, what peace could there ever be for my heart?

sanskrit: nāsmiñ jātu kule jāto gacched yo 'nyasya pṛṣṭhataḥ na tvaṃ parasyānudhuraṃ tāta jīvitum arhasi
english: Never has one born in this lineage walked behind another. You, my dear, have no right to live as a lesser yoke-bearer under someone else.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi kṣatrahṛdayaṃ veda yat pariśāśvatam pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraiḥ proktaṃ paraiḥ paratarair api
english: For I know the eternal heart of the kṣatriya, as proclaimed by the forefathers and by those before them, and by those who came still later.

sanskrit: yo vai kaś cid ihājātaḥ kṣatriyaḥ kṣatradharmavit bhayād vṛttisamīkṣo vā na named iha kasya cit
english: Whatever kṣatriya is born in this world and knows the duty of his class — whether out of fear or in quest of a livelihood — he should bow down to no one here.

sanskrit: udyacched eva na named udyamo hy eva pauruṣam apy aparvaṇi bhajyeta na named iha kasya cit
english: He must rise up and not bow; for rising up is itself manliness. Even if he breaks at the wrong moment, let him not bow to anyone here.

sanskrit: mātaṅgo matta iva ca parīyāt sumahāmanāḥ brāhmaṇebhyo namen nityaṃ dharmāyaiva ca saṃjaya
english: Like a rutting elephant, let him move about with a most exalted spirit; let him bow always to brahmins and to righteousness alone, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: niyacchann itarān varṇān vinighnan sarvaduṣkṛtaḥ sasahāyo 'sahāyo vā yāvajjīvaṃ tathā bhavet
english: Restraining the other social orders, striking down all wrongdoers — whether with allies or without — let him be thus for as long as he lives.

sanskrit: putra uvāca kṛṣṇāyasasyeva ca te saṃhatya hṛdayaṃ kṛtam mama mātas tv akaruṇe vairaprajñe hy amarṣaṇe
english: The son said: You have fashioned your heart as though of black iron, O Mother — pitiless, wise in enmity, and filled with wrath.

sanskrit: aho kṣatrasamācāro yatra mām aparaṃ yathā īdṛśaṃ vacanaṃ brūyād bhavatī putram ekajam
english: Ah, such is the conduct of the kṣatriya — that you would speak such words to me, your only son, as though to a stranger!

sanskrit: kiṃ nu te mām apaśyantyāḥ pṛthivyā api sarvayā kim ābharaṇakṛtyaṃ te kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā
english: What good is all the earth to you if you cannot see me? What use are ornaments to you? What use are pleasures, or life itself?

sanskrit: mātovāca sarvārambhā hi viduṣāṃ tāta dharmārthakāraṇāt tān evābhisamīkṣyāhaṃ saṃjaya tvām acūcudam
english: The mother said: All undertakings of the wise, my dear, are for the sake of righteousness and gain. Keeping exactly those aims in view, Sañjaya, I have urged you on.

sanskrit: sa samīkṣyakramopeto mukhyaḥ kālo 'yam āgataḥ asmiṃś ced āgate kāle kāryaṃ na pratipadyase asaṃbhāvitarūpas tvaṃ sunṛśaṃsaṃ kariṣyasi
english: This is the foremost moment, full of judicious opportunity, that has arrived. If, when this moment has come, you do not take up the task, you — a man of unproven worth — will act very cruelly.

sanskrit: taṃ tvām ayaśasā spṛṣṭaṃ na brūyāṃ yadi saṃjaya kharīvātsalyam āhus tan niḥsāmarthyam ahetukam
english: If I did not speak to you when you are touched by disgrace, Sañjaya, they would call that the affection of a she-ass — helplessness disguised as love, without reason.

sanskrit: sadbhir vigarhitaṃ mārgaṃ tyaja mūrkhaniṣevitam avidyā vai mahaty asti yām imāṃ saṃśritāḥ prajāḥ
english: Abandon the path condemned by the good and frequented by fools. There is a great ignorance, and the people who have taken refuge in it are many.

sanskrit: tava syād yadi sadvṛttaṃ tena me tvaṃ priyo bhaveḥ dharmārthaguṇayuktena netareṇa kathaṃ cana daivamānuṣayuktena sadbhir ācaritena ca
english: If you were to have right conduct, you would be dear to me by that alone — by conduct endowed with righteousness, wealth, and virtue; not by any other means; conduct joined with divine and human qualities and practised by the good.

sanskrit: yo hy evam avinītena ramate putranaptṛṇā anutthānavatā cāpi moghaṃ tasya prajāphalam
english: He who takes pleasure in sons and grandsons who are thus ill-disciplined and without the impulse to rise — for him, the fruit of offspring is barren.

sanskrit: akurvanto hi karmāṇi kurvanto ninditāni ca sukhaṃ naiveha nāmutra labhante puruṣādhamāḥ
english: Those lowest of men who neither do what ought to be done, nor do what is blamed for being done, find no happiness — neither here nor in the hereafter.

sanskrit: yuddhāya kṣatriyaḥ sṛṣṭaḥ saṃjayeha jayāya ca krūrāya karmaṇe nityaṃ prajānāṃ paripālane jayan vā vadhyamāno vā prāpnotīndrasalokatām
english: The kṣatriya is created for battle and for victory, Sañjaya; for fierce deeds and forever for the protection of subjects. Whether he conquers or is slain, he attains to the world of Indra.

sanskrit: na śakrabhavane puṇye divi tad vidyate sukham yad amitrān vaśe kṛtvā kṣatriyaḥ sukham aśnute
english: Not even in the sacred abode of Śakra in heaven does there exist such happiness as a kṣatriya enjoys when he brings his enemies under his power.

sanskrit: manyunā dahyamānena puruṣeṇa manasvinā nikṛteneha bahuśaḥ śatrūn pratijigīṣayā
english: For a high-minded man burning with wrath, deceived repeatedly here, with the desire to conquer his enemies —

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ vā parityajya śatrūn vā vinipātya vai ato 'nyena prakāreṇa śāntir asya kuto bhavet
english: — either by abandoning himself entirely, or by laying his enemies low — by any means other than these, where can peace come to him?

sanskrit: iha prājño hi puruṣaḥ svalpam apriyam icchati yasya svalpaṃ priyaṃ loke dhruvaṃ tasyālpam apriyam
english: A wise man in this world wills only a little that is unpleasant; he whose pleasure in the world is small — for him, certainly, the unpleasant too is small.

sanskrit: priyābhāvāc ca puruṣo naiva prāpnoti śobhanam dhruvaṃ cābhāvam abhyeti gatvā gaṅgeva sāgaram
english: Without the pleasant, a man never obtains what is beautiful; and he who avoids action certainly moves toward non-existence, as the Gaṅgā goes to the ocean.

sanskrit: putra uvāca neyaṃ matis tvayā vācyā mātaḥ putre viśeṣataḥ kāruṇyam evātra paśya bhūtveha jaḍamūkavat
english: The son said: This reasoning should not be spoken by you, Mother — especially not to a son. See only compassion here; be here like one dumb and dull.

sanskrit: mātovāca ato me bhūyasī nandir yad evam anupaśyasi codyaṃ māṃ codayasy etad bhṛśaṃ vai codayāmi te
english: The mother said: This delights me all the more — that you perceive the urging this way and urge me with it; it is precisely this that I urge upon you most strongly.

sanskrit: atha tvāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi hatvā vai sarvasaindhavān ahaṃ paśyāmi vijayaṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhāvinam eva te
english: Then I shall honour you — after you have slain all the Saindhava forces. I see complete and certain victory coming to you.

sanskrit: putra uvāca akośasyāsahāyasya kutaḥ svid vijayo mama ity avasthāṃ viditvemām ātmanātmani dāruṇām rājyād bhāvo nivṛtto me tridivād iva duṣkṛteḥ
english: The son said: Without a treasury, without allies — how indeed can victory be mine? Knowing this harsh condition within myself, my attachment to the kingdom has left me, as a sinner is cut off from heaven.

sanskrit: īdṛśaṃ bhavatī kaṃ cid upāyam anupaśyati tan me pariṇataprajñe samyak prabrūhi pṛcchate kariṣyāmi hi tat sarvaṃ yathāvad anuśāsanam
english: If you, O ripened in wisdom, see some means out of a situation like this, tell me it fully, for I am asking; I will do all of it exactly according to your instruction.

sanskrit: mātovāca putrātmā nāvamantavyaḥ pūrvābhir asamṛddhibhiḥ abhūtvā hi bhavanty arthā bhūtvā naśyanti cāpare
english: The mother said: One who is the soul of his son should not be underestimated on account of earlier failures. Things that did not exist come into being; and things that exist perish.

sanskrit: amarṣeṇaiva cāpy arthā nārabdhavyāḥ subāliśaiḥ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ tāta phale nityam anityatā
english: Nor should affairs be undertaken by the very young through impatience alone. In the fruit of all actions, my dear, there is always impermanence.

sanskrit: anityam iti jānanto na bhavanti bhavanti ca atha ye naiva kurvanti naiva jātu bhavanti te
english: Those who know that things are impermanent — they sometimes fail to prosper, and they sometimes prosper. But those who never act — they never prosper at all.

sanskrit: aikaguṇyam anīhāyām abhāvaḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam atha dvaiguṇyam īhāyāṃ phalaṃ bhavati vā na vā
english: In the absence of effort, there is only one possibility — the non-occurrence of the fruit of action. With effort, there are two possibilities — the fruit may or may not come.

sanskrit: yasya prāg eva viditā sarvārthānām anityatā nuded vṛddhisamṛddhī sa pratikūle nṛpātmaja
english: He who has understood beforehand the impermanence of all things will drive forward prosperity and success even in adverse circumstances, O son of a king.

sanskrit: utthātavyaṃ jāgṛtavyaṃ yoktavyaṃ bhūtikarmasu bhaviṣyatīty eva manaḥ kṛtvā satatam avyathaiḥ maṅgalāni puraskṛtya brāhmaṇaiś ceśvaraiḥ saha
english: One must rise up, keep vigil, and apply oneself to acts of prosperity — keeping the mind always fixed on 'it shall be so' without faltering, placing auspicious rites foremost, and acting together with brahmins and men of power.

sanskrit: prājñasya nṛpater āśu vṛddhir bhavati putraka abhivartati lakṣmīs taṃ prācīm iva divākaraḥ
english: For the wise king, prosperity comes swiftly, my boy; Lakṣmī advances toward him as the sun advances toward the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: nidarśanāny upāyāṃś ca bahūny uddharṣaṇāni ca anudarśitarūpo 'si paśyāmi kuru pauruṣam puruṣārtham abhipretaṃ samāhartum ihārhasi
english: Many examples, means, and encouragements have been shown to you; your true form has been made visible to you. I see it — perform your manliness; you are fit to gather here the human goal you have in mind.

sanskrit: kruddhāṃl lubdhān parikṣīṇān avakṣiptān vimānitān spardhinaś caiva ye ke cit tān yukta upadhāraya
english: The wrathful, the greedy, the exhausted, the overlooked, the dishonoured, and the rivals — whoever they may be — regard them with a fitting eye and hold them fast.

sanskrit: etena tvaṃ prakāreṇa mahato bhetsyase gaṇān mahāvega ivoddhūto mātariśvā balāhakān
english: By this method you will split apart great hosts, just as the wind, rising with mighty force, scatters the rain clouds.

sanskrit: teṣām agrapradāyī syāḥ kalyotthāyī priyaṃvadaḥ te tvāṃ priyaṃ kariṣyanti puro dhāsyanti ca dhruvam
english: Be the first to give them gifts; be one who rises early and speaks pleasant words. They will make you dear to them and will surely place you at their fore.

sanskrit: yadaiva śatrur jānīyāt sapatnaṃ tyaktajīvitam tadaivāsmād udvijate sarpād veśmagatād iva
english: The very moment an enemy knows his rival has cast aside all care for his life, he recoils from him — just as from a serpent that has entered the house.

sanskrit: taṃ viditvā parākrāntaṃ vaśe na kurute yadi nirvādair nirvaded enam antatas tad bhaviṣyati
english: If, knowing him to be bold and aggressive, the enemy does not bring him under control, he will wear him down with reproaches — and in the end that will come to pass.

sanskrit: nirvādād āspadaṃ labdhvā dhanavṛddhir bhaviṣyati dhanavantaṃ hi mitrāṇi bhajante cāśrayanti ca
english: Having gained a foothold through wearing the enemy down, wealth will grow; for it is the wealthy man whom friends seek out and lean upon.

sanskrit: skhalitārthaṃ punas tāta saṃtyajanty api bāndhavāḥ apy asminn āśrayante ca jugupsanti ca tādṛśam
english: When a man stumbles in his affairs, my dear, even kinsmen abandon him; and in that same state, they both take shelter with him and despise him — such is the way of things.

sanskrit: śatruṃ kṛtvā yaḥ sahāyaṃ viśvāsam upagacchati ataḥ saṃbhāvyam evaitad yad rājyaṃ prāpnuyād iti
english: He who, having made an enemy into an ally, places trust in him — it is precisely from this that the recovery of the kingdom is to be expected.

sanskrit: mātovāca naiva rājñā daraḥ kāryo jātu kasyāṃ cid āpadi atha ced api dīrṇaḥ syān naiva varteta dīrṇavat
english: The mother said: A king should never show fear in any adversity whatsoever. And even if he is shattered, he should not conduct himself like one who is shattered.

sanskrit: dīrṇaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ sarvam evānudīryate rāṣṭraṃ balam amātyāś ca pṛthak kurvanti te matim
english: For seeing a king shattered, everything shatters in turn; the kingdom, the army, and the ministers each take their minds elsewhere.

sanskrit: śatrūn eke prapadyante prajahaty apare punaḥ anv eke prajihīrṣanti ye purastād vimānitāḥ
english: Some go over to the enemies; others simply desert; and yet others — those who were humiliated before — now seek to do him harm in turn.

sanskrit: ya evātyantasuhṛdas ta enaṃ paryupāsate aśaktayaḥ svastikāmā baddhavatsā iḍā iva śocantam anuśocanti pratītān iva bāndhavān
english: Only those who are his truest friends gather around him — powerless themselves, wishing him well, like cows bound to their calves; they grieve for him in his grief, as kinsmen mourn for the departed.

sanskrit: api te pūjitāḥ pūrvam api te suhṛdo matāḥ ye rāṣṭram abhimanyante rājño vyasanam īyuṣaḥ mā dīdaras tvaṃ suhṛdo mā tvāṃ dīrṇaṃ prahāsiṣuḥ
english: Even those who were previously honoured by you, even those regarded as your friends — who now covet the kingdom of a king who has fallen into misfortune — do not let your friends see you shattered; do not let them abandon you as one broken.
